text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"application_screening_fees","status":"in_force","title":"California cap and conditions on application screening fees","requirement":"Landlords may charge an application screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering applicant information (e.g., tenant screening service, credit report) plus the reasonable value of time spent, never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually with CPI beginning Jan. 1, 1998). No fee may be charged if the landlord knows or should have known no unit is or will soon be available. A fee may be charged only if the landlord offers either (A) a first-come, first-served screening process with written screening criteria provided with the application, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and no fee charged unless the application is actually considered (inadvertent concurrent collections refunded within 7 days, or applied to another unit at the applicant's option; no refund required if denied after consideration for failing the criteria), or (B) return of the entire fee to any applicant not selected, within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days of application submission, whichever is first. The landlord must give a itemized receipt (by personal delivery, mail, or agreed email), return any unused portion if no reference check or credit report is obtained, and provide a copy of the credit report to the applicant within 7 days of receiving it. Landlords may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.","key_value":"$30 per applicant maximum (CPI-adjustable annually since Jan. 1, 1998); refunds within 7 days","coverage_conditions":"Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants (including guarantors/cosigners) for residential rental units.","exemptions":"Not intended to preempt provisions or regulations governing collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":null},"subject":"landlord","interaction":"Applies notwithstanding Section 1950.5; the fee is not an 'advance fee' under Bus. & Prof. Code § 10026 nor 'security' under Civ.
